1. ROW-LEVEL CORRECTNESS (factual) — PASS, fully source-verified.
Both Wikipedia pages independently confirm every row and every adoption year:
- Founding members, 1 Jan 1999 (cited source verbatim: “the first 11 (Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Spain) introduced the euro on 1 January 1999”). All 11 present in CSV with year 1999. EXACT name match.
- Greece 2001, Slovenia 2007, Cyprus 2008, Malta 2008, Slovakia 2009, Estonia 2011, Latvia 2014, Lithuania 2015, Croatia 2023 — all present, all years correct against both sources.
- No incorrect, duplicate, or unsupported rows. Per-cell Adoption Year accuracy: 20/20 correct.

2. EXHAUSTIVE / SCOPE — PASS (claim is load-bearing and justified).
- The query universe (eurozone member states + accession years) is an authoritatively-defined CLOSED set, not a “notable examples” subset. Per claude_4.8_dataset_curaiton_draft.md, claim_type=exhaustive means “the sources authoritatively define a closed set” — which holds here. The Eurozone validation page confirms Croatia is the 20th member and the last within [1999, 2023]; Bulgaria is the 21st (2026). So 20 rows is EXACTLY the in-range membership — no more, no less.
- Boundary exclusion (scope): Bulgaria 2026 is in both sources but correctly EXCLUDED (out of [1999, 2023] range). Confirmed.
- Non-member euro users (scope): The cited page frames Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City, Andorra under “Outside the EU → European microstates” using “monetary agreements,” and Kosovo/Montenegro as having “unilaterally adopted” the euro. The source framing supports excluding all six as non-members. Correctly EXCLUDED.
- Future EU members bound to adopt (Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Sweden) have no committed dates and have not adopted — correctly excluded.

3. DUPLICATES / PRIMARY KEY (structural) — PASS. PK=Country; all 20 country names unique; no duplicate composite key; no near-duplicate entities.

4. NORMALIZATION / TABLE SHAPE / COLUMN TYPES (structural) — PASS. Country=key (single canonical English article name per row; “Netherlands” canonical for source’s “the Netherlands”). Adoption Year=numeric (bare 4-digit integers, all conform). One value per cell; no multi-valued cells.

5. CARDINALITY / PARTITION SANITY — PASS. 20 rows, 20 unique keys. Distribution matches source-defined accession history: 11 (1999) + 1 (2001) + 1 (2007) + 2 (2008) + 1 (2009) + 1 (2011) + 1 (2014) + 1 (2015) + 1 (2023) = 20. Not a partitioned/ranked instance, so no per-partition top-K convention to check. Clears the 10-row minimum (curation_protocol.md §5.2).

6. PREFLIGHT (structural) — PASS. Row count = 20 (excl header). CSV header ‘Country,Adoption Year’ == draft.json columns. PK unique. Sort order matches db_analog ORDER BY adoption_year, country (verified by diff against a re-sorted copy: identical).

The cited ‘Enlargement of the eurozone’ page is the most direct Wikipedia list/table page for this query (it is the dedicated accession-history page, not a mere entity/overview page). The ‘Eurozone’ page is a sibling that fully corroborates and is recorded here as a validation source only; it does not need to be added to source_urls to defend the row set or scope. No redirect/See-also/Wikidata gap found that would change the row universe, ranking, or boundary.

8. SOURCE ROLE / source_count=1 (scope) — PASS. The single cited source plays the ‘universe’ role and supports BOTH the full exhaustive membership list AND every adoption year. source_count=1 is honest and sufficient.

9. METADATA / cfg CORRECTNESS (structural) — PASS.
- query_category=temporal (valid; categories.txt: ‘WHERE year BETWEEN x AND y’), secondary_category=set_filter (valid).
- operation_type=filter — valid per curation_protocol.md vocabulary (‘single-source with a WHERE predicate (set_filter, temporal, geographic)’).
- primary_key=[Country], column_types Country=key / Adoption Year=numeric — correct.
- db_analog matches the CSV (BETWEEN 1999 AND 2023, ORDER BY adoption_year, country) — ordering verified.
- source_count=1, gt_construction=manual_wikipedia, temporal_sensitivity=low — appropriate (historical accession facts are stable; the only post-cutoff change, Bulgaria 2026, is outside scope, so low is correct).
- temporal_note and _extraction_notes accurately describe the 1999–2023 filter and the single intentional exclusion (Bulgaria). curation.json claim_type=exhaustive with a documented decision_log (initial 2001–2023 draft had 9 rows < 10-row minimum, widened to 1999–2023 → 20). All consistent.

Not one of the listed example subdomains, but the taxonomy explicitly discourages churn on understandable labels. NON-BLOCKING at most; I do not flag it.

Eurozone membership and accession years are firmly in LLM parametric knowledge yet require correct temporal-range filtering and exclusion of look-alike non-members — a clean, easily-auditable temporal/set_filter item.
